content: When amlodipine is coadministered with CYP3A inhibitors, it may necessitate a reduction in dosage. Patients should be monitored for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine if dose adjustments are required. Both clarithromycin and levofloxacin can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored in such cases. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. The maximum daily dose of levomilnacipran should not exceed 80 mg when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor metabolism is affected by hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Due to the induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A, the net exposure of ivacaftor at steady state is not expected to exceed that of ivacaftor monotherapy at the approved dose of 150 mg every 12 hours. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients already taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, the dose should be reduced to one tablet daily (lumacaftor 200 mg/ivacaftor 125 mg total daily dose) for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. After this period, the recommended daily dose can be resumed. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor is a strong CYP3A4 inducer and has the potential to induce CYP2C19 and both induce and inhibit P-glycoprotein. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. The dose of lumateperone should not exceed 5 mg/day when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Omeprazole increases methotrexate levels by decreasing renal clearance. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Temporary withdrawal of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) may be considered in some patients. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. The maraviroc dose should be reduced to 150 mg twice daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Clarithromycin also increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of marijuana by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mavorizxafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Both mavorizxafor and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. QTc monitoring is recommended during treatment, especially in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation, such as coadministered medications that increase mavorizxafor exposure or other drugs with a high risk of QTc prolongation. Clarithromycin also increases mavorizxafor levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Clarithromycin also increases mestranol levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin and methadone both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Omeprazole decreases the effects of methylphenidate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral form of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Since the characteristics of methylphenidate extended-release capsules (Ritalin LA) are pH-dependent, coadministration of antacids or acid suppressants could alter the release of methylphenidate. Consider separating the administration of the antacid and the methylphenidate extended-release capsules. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Coadministration of mild CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam may cause higher systemic exposure to midazolam, potentially prolonging sedation. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. The daily dose of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome should not exceed 300 mg when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. This combination may also prolong the QT interval. Alternatives should be considered if available. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4 (a CYP3A4 substrate and the cytotoxic component of the antibody-drug conjugate for mirvetuximab soravtansine), potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Mitotane decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Mitotane is a strong inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4; monitoring is advised when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates for potential dosage adjustments. Modafinil increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of momelotinib through mechanisms involving OATP1B1/B3 inhibition, which increases momelotinib plasma concentrations and may heighten the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of inhaled mometasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as this interaction increases the risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects.
